text:
priya: Heads up — CVE-2026-0421 reported affecting golang.org/x/oauth2 token parsing and grpc server auth interceptors (grpc v1.52+). Can we triage impact and patch plan?

kevin: Do we have POC/repro? What parts of our stack use oauth2 directly vs transitively? Any net/http involvement?

priya: quick scan: services using oauth2 client libs: auth-service, token-mgmt, internal-cli. grpc usage in runtime-proxy and model-ingest. Repro attached in GH issue (link omitted). Looks like malformed token headers can cause header parse panic in oauth2 and auth interceptor bypass in specific edgecases.

elaine: Recommend immediate pin in go.mod for oauth2 to v0.0.0-20260201 and grpc to v1.53.1 (patched). Example:
```
require (
  golang.org/x/oauth2 v0.0.0-20260201
  google.golang.org/grpc v1.53.1
)
```
Pin in a release branch and open hotfix PRs.

ben: Agree. We'll need a hotpatch pipeline: branch -> internal CI -> canary (10% traffic on Dedicated and Hosted) -> 50% -> full. That gives rollback points. Also note Dedicated nodes use KMS for token signing; coordinate KMS key rotation windows with infra.

priya: Priority=P1 due to auth bypass risk. Plan to create hotpatch branches for master and release-2024, run smoke e2e, and schedule canary tonight UTC 02:00. If any failures rollback to previous image.

kevin: Also add a runtime guard: reject tokens with unexpected header shapes and log to audit. Quick patch snippet to add defensive check in interceptor.

elaine: We should also add an alert on increased token parse errors and failed auth counts in the last 15m. Ops runbook updated to include KMS audit checks and RBAC review for token admin perms.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline for PR #3482 passed all checks and created canary deploy job at 1965012380.

priya: TL;DR: hotpatch PRs opened, go.mod pinned, canary scheduled, monitoring+audit logging added. I'll follow up with rollback playbook and CVE report. :thumbsup:
